payload.task_text:
I need to review our product ratings and set up a feedback process for our underperforming products. Please look at all products in our store that have customer reviews and find the five products with the lowest average ratings. If there are ties in average rating, prefer products with more reviews.

For these five lowest-rated products, create a Google Form titled Product Quality Improvement Survey with a description explaining that we are gathering customer feedback to improve product quality. For each of the five products, add a required rating question asking customers to rate their overall satisfaction with that product on a scale of one to five, using the product name in the question text. Implement each rating question as a single-choice (multiple choice) question whose options are the five values 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and set it as required. Also add one optional text question at the end asking for additional suggestions for improvement.

Create an Excel file called Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx with a sheet called Review Summary that lists all reviewed products, one row per product, with columns for Product_Name truncated to sixty characters, Avg_Rating rounded to two decimal places, Review_Count, and Category using the first category name from each product. Sort by Avg_Rating in ascending order. Add a second sheet called Stats with Metric and Value rows for Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product with the product name truncated to forty characters, and Avg_Rating_Overall as the average rating across all reviewed products rounded to two decimal places. Write all numeric values (Avg_Rating, Review_Count, Total_Products_Reviewed, Avg_Rating_Overall) as literal numbers, not spreadsheet formulas.

Schedule a product quality review meeting in the calendar on March 20 2026 from 2pm to 3pm with the title Product Quality Review Meeting.

Send an email to product.team@company.com with subject Product Quality Alert - Review Required mentioning the names of the five lowest-rated products and requesting the team to review them.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one read-only Explore wave for the 82-product/396-review store join, then one writer wave with two parallel coder sub-agents. No plan agent is used: the frozen payload between the waves is the complete plan.

Dynamically resolve the workspace and freeze the ranking contract: every product with at least one review, ranked by average rating ascending, review count descending, then stable Product_ID; the five lowest define the survey, meeting and email. Start the fixed-date event inventory independently.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 Explore sub-agent (read-only):

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Review gatherer: paginate both store endpoints with perPage=100 and increasing page until a short or empty page, omitting review status and preserving observed statuses. Join strictly on Product_ID; for every product with at least one review compute the literal Review_Count and the average rating (full precision, 2-decimal display), keeping the full product name and the first category. Select the lowest five by average rating ascending, review count descending, then stable Product_ID. Return only the complete reviewed-products table (id, full name, avg_rating, review_count, first category), the frozen five-row ranking with complete product names, record counts, duplicate IDs, and page controls — no writes, no full item arrays.

After Wave 1, verify the handoff in one single pass: row count equals the product join, every reviewed product covered, five-row ranking unambiguous. The main agent then freezes one canonical product_review_data.json in the workspace containing: the products list (82 objects with id, full name, avg_rating 2 decimals, review_count, category), the frozen bottom-five ranking with complete names, and the Stats values (Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product truncated to forty characters, Avg_Rating_Overall rounded to two decimals). This file is the single binding input for Wave 2; nobody re-reads the store afterwards.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming product_review_data.json verbatim with no recomputation and no store reads:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Workbook writer — sole writer of Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx. Create it exactly once with exactly two sheets: Review Summary with columns Product_Name (truncated to sixty characters), Avg_Rating (two decimals), Review_Count, Category (first category), one row per reviewed product sorted by Avg_Rating ascending; Stats with columns Metric, Value and rows Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product (truncated to forty characters), Avg_Rating_Overall (two decimals). Write all numeric values as literal numbers, never formulas; read both populated ranges back and return path, sheet order, row counts and equality controls.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): External writer — sole owner of form, event and email. Forms has no list/search: call create_form exactly once titled Product Quality Improvement Survey with the stated description, never retry an ambiguous failure, then append sequentially on that one formId five add_multiple_choice_question calls in frozen rank order, each using the product name in the question text with options ["1","2","3","4","5"] and required=true, followed by one add_text_question(..., required=false) for additional suggestions; call get_form and verify title/description/question order/types/options/flags. Filter list_events(timeMin="2026-03-20T00:00:00", timeMax="2026-03-21T00:00:00", maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime") locally for the exact Product Quality Review Meeting at 14:00-15:00; create it once only if missing with exact start.dateTime/end.dateTime, retain the ID, and call get_event. Paginate Sent search for product.team@company.com and exact subject Product Quality Alert - Review Required, send at most once naming the frozen five products, then read it back.

After Wave 2, verify both handoffs in one single pass against product_review_data.json: workbook cell-for-cell, five-question form structure, event identity, and email contents. Accept only after every read-back matches the frozen payload, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent after Wave 2.

nodes.text:
You are a read-only data analyst working against a WooCommerce store API. Your job is to gather product review data and produce a frozen ranking of the five lowest-rated products. DO NOT write anything, do not create files, do not modify any store data — read-only exploration only.

CONTEXT: The parent agent needs to (a) build an Excel analysis workbook, (b) build a Google Form with 5 rating questions, (c) schedule a calendar meeting, (d) send an email — all driven by the five products with the lowest average customer ratings. Your output is the single source of truth for that.

TASK:
1. List ALL products in the store by paginating mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list with perPage=100, starting at page=1 and increasing the page number until you get a short page (fewer than 100 results) or an empty page. Record the total number of products and any duplicate product IDs you see across pages. For each product, keep its id, full name, and categories (the categories array — you only need the FIRST category name per product; a product may have zero categories, in which case category is empty string).

2. For EVERY product, fetch its reviews via mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_reviews_list with productId=<id>, perPage=100, status="approved", paginating pages until short/empty. NOTE: also try status="all" if "approved" returns zero but reviews may exist — but prefer approved (the store's visible customer reviews). Actually, follow this rule: use status="approved" first; if a product returns 0 reviews with "approved", try status="all" once to check whether non-approved reviews exist, and note the observed statuses in your report. Count reviews per product (Review_Count) and compute the average rating across that product's approved reviews at FULL precision (sum of ratings / count). A product with zero approved reviews is NOT part of the reviewed-products table.

3. Build the complete reviewed-products table: every product with at least one approved review, with columns: product id, full product name (untruncated), avg_rating (full precision float — keep at least 6 decimal places internally), review_count (integer), first category name (or empty string).

4. Select the FIVE lowest-rated products by this exact tie-breaking rule, in priority order:
   a. avg_rating ascending (lowest first)
   b. review_count descending (more reviews preferred on ties in avg_rating)
   c. stable product id ascending (lowest id first) as final tiebreak
   This gives a fully deterministic ranking. The result is the frozen bottom-five ranking.

5. Also compute: Total_Products_Reviewed = number of products with >= 1 approved review; the lowest-rated product's name (full, untruncated — parent will truncate to 40 chars); Avg_Rating_Overall = average of avg_rating across ALL reviewed products (i.e., mean of per-product average ratings), full precision (parent rounds to 2 decimals).

RETURN IN YOUR FINAL REPORT (this is the deliverable — be exact and complete):
- Record counts: total products fetched, total pages per endpoint, number of products with 0 reviews, number of reviewed products.
- Any duplicate product IDs observed and any anomalies (e.g., products whose reviews endpoint failed/errored — retry once, and if it still fails, say so explicitly with the product id).
- The complete reviewed-products table as a JSON array of objects: {"id": <int>, "name": "<full name>", "avg_rating": <float full precision>, "review_count": <int>, "category": "<first category or empty>"}. Include EVERY reviewed product — this is the full table, not a sample.
- The frozen five-row ranking: the 5 selected products, each with id, full untruncated name, avg_rating (full precision), review_count, category, and rank position 1-5.
- Total_Products_Reviewed and Avg_Rating_Overall (full precision).
- Your pagination page controls (final page numbers used for products and for each review fetch pattern) so the parent can verify completeness.

Be exhaustive and precise — the parent will trust this data verbatim without re-reading the store. Do not truncate product names in your report.
Review gatherer: products + ratings

You are the SOLE writer of an Excel workbook. Work read-only against a frozen JSON payload; do NOT recompute ratings, do NOT query the store, do NOT modify anything else.

CONTEXT: A parent agent already gathered product review data from a WooCommerce store and froze the canonical payload at:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace/product_review_data.json

The JSON has this exact structure (trust it verbatim, do not recompute):
- "products": list of 82 objects {"id": int, "name": full product name, "avg_rating": float already rounded to 2 decimals, "review_count": int, "category": first category name or ""}
- "bottom_five": list of 5 objects {"rank": 1-5, "id", "name", "avg_rating", "avg_rating_rounded", "review_count", "category"}
- "stats": {"total_products_reviewed": 82, "lowest_rated_product": "<40-char truncated name>", "avg_rating_overall": 4.62}

DELIVERABLE: Create exactly one Excel file at
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace/Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx
using the mcp__excel__ tools (create_workbook, rename_worksheet/create_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, read_data_from_excel). The workbook must contain EXACTLY TWO sheets, in this order:

1. Sheet named "Review Summary":
   - Row 1 header: Product_Name | Avg_Rating | Review_Count | Category
   - One row per product (all 82), sorted by Avg_Rating ASCENDING (lowest first). For ties in Avg_Rating, sort by Review_Count descending, then by product id ascending (deterministic).
   - Product_Name: full name truncated to 60 characters (Python-style slice [:60])
   - Avg_Rating: the numeric value (2 decimals) as a LITERAL NUMBER — never a formula
   - Review_Count: literal integer number
   - Category: first category name (may be empty string)

2. Sheet named "Stats":
   - Row 1 header: Metric | Value
   - Row 2: Total_Products_Reviewed | 82 (literal number)
   - Row 3: Lowest_Rated_Product | <the "lowest_rated_product" string from stats, already truncated to 40 chars>
   - Row 4: Avg_Rating_Overall | 4.62 (literal number, from stats.avg_rating_overall)
   - All numeric values as LITERAL NUMBERS, never formulas.

STEPS:
1. create_workbook at the target path (this creates a default sheet — rename it to "Review Summary", then create the second worksheet "Stats"; ensure no third/extra sheets remain, and sheet order is Review Summary then Stats).
2. Write Review Summary data (header + 82 rows) starting at A1.
3. Write Stats data (header + 3 rows) starting at A1.
4. Read BOTH populated ranges back with read_data_from_excel and verify cell-by-cell against the JSON: 82 data rows in Review Summary, correct sort order (avg ascending), every product present exactly once, Avg_Rating and Review_Count numeric (not strings/formulas), Stats rows exact.

RETURN IN YOUR FINAL REPORT:
- Absolute path of the created workbook
- Sheet order and names (confirm exactly 2 sheets)
- Row counts per sheet (header + data)
- The equality/verification controls you ran (e.g., matched every product id/rating/count, sort order monotonic check)
- Any deviations (must be none)
Do NOT create the file anywhere else and do NOT touch any other files.
Workbook writer: Review Analysis xlsx

You are the SOLE owner of three external-system writes: a Google Form, a Google Calendar event, and an email. Work read-only against a frozen JSON payload; do NOT recompute rankings, do NOT query the store.

CONTEXT: A parent agent already computed the five lowest-rated products in a WooCommerce store and froze the canonical payload at:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace/product_review_data.json

Relevant structure (trust verbatim):
- "bottom_five": list of exactly 5 objects in frozen rank order 1-5, each {"rank": 1-5, "id": int, "name": full untruncated product name, "avg_rating": float, "avg_rating_rounded": float, "review_count": int, "category": str}
Use the "name" field (full, untruncated) wherever product names are needed.

PART A — GOOGLE FORM (mcp__google_forms__*):
1. Call create_form EXACTLY ONCE with title "Product Quality Improvement Survey" and a description explaining that we are gathering customer feedback to improve product quality (e.g., "We are gathering customer feedback to improve the quality of our products. Please take a moment to share your experience."). Keep the exact title as given. Do NOT retry ambiguous failures — if the call fails, report the failure and stop this part.
2. Using the returned formId, append sequentially (in frozen rank order 1→5) FIVE add_multiple_choice_question calls, one per bottom-five product. For each: questionTitle must ask customers to rate their overall satisfaction with that product on a scale of one to five AND include the product's full name in the text (e.g., "How would you rate your overall satisfaction with <PRODUCT NAME> on a scale of 1 to 5?"), options must be exactly ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"], required=true.
3. After the five rating questions, add ONE add_text_question (required=false) asking for additional suggestions for improvement (e.g., "Do you have any additional suggestions for improvement?").
4. Verify with get_form on that formId: confirm title, description, exactly 6 questions in order (5 multiple-choice rating questions in rank order with the right options and required=true, then 1 text question required=false). Report the formId and the verification.

PART B — GOOGLE CALENDAR EVENT (mcp__google_calendar__*):
1. Call list_events with timeMin="2026-03-20T00:00:00", timeMax="2026-03-21T00:00:00", maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime". Filter the returned events locally for the exact event "Product Quality Review Meeting" starting at 14:00 and ending at 15:00 on 2026-03-20.
2. If such an event already exists, keep its ID and do NOT create another. If it does NOT exist, create it EXACTLY ONCE with summary "Product Quality Review Meeting", start.dateTime="2026-03-20T14:00:00", end.dateTime="2026-03-20T15:00:00" (retain the returned event id).
3. Call get_event with the retained id to verify summary and start/end datetimes. Report the event id and verification.

PART C — EMAIL (mcp__emails__*):
1. Check whether an email to product.team@company.com with the exact subject "Product Quality Alert - Review Required" already exists: search_emails(query="Product Quality Alert - Review Required", folder="Sent", page_size=50, and paginate) and also check INBOX if needed. 
2. If none exists, send EXACTLY ONCE via send_email: to="product.team@company.com", subject="Product Quality Alert - Review Required", body that (a) names the five lowest-rated products (full names, in frozen rank order) and (b) requests the team to review them (e.g., "The following products have the lowest average customer ratings and require review: 1. ... 2. ... Please review these products and take action to improve their quality.").
3. Read the sent email back (search Sent for the subject, read it) to confirm recipient, subject, and that all five product names appear in the body.

RETURN IN YOUR FINAL REPORT:
- Form ID + confirmed title/description/question count/order/types/options/required flags
- Calendar event ID + confirmed summary/start/end
- Email confirmation: sent once, recipient, subject, body contains all five product names (list them)
- Any deviations (must be none), or exact failure messages if a step failed
Do NOT create duplicate forms/events/emails and do NOT touch any other systems.
External writer: form, event, email
